# Alpha Fresh Co., Ltd. (บริษัท อัลฟ่า เฟรช จำกัด)

> A small Thai fruit business in Lamphun, Northern Thailand. Originally an
> importer of fresh fruit, now exporting Thai fruit outward using the same
> cold room, refrigerated truck and customs know-how. Flagship product:
> fresh longan. Also durian, mangosteen and lychee in season.

Contact: alphafreshthailand@gmail.com · +66 89 894 9491 (also LINE and WeChat)
Languages: Thai and English (both on every page, switched with the TH/EN toggle)
Terms: EXW, FOB, CFR, CIF (Incoterms 2020)

## Products

- **Fresh longan (ลำไย)** — flagship. Varieties: E-Daw (main export variety),
  Daw, Biew Kiew. Grown in Lamphun, Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai; off-season
  fruit from Chanthaburi. In season July–September (peak August); off-season
  November–February. Grades AA (≥26 mm), A (24–26 mm), B (22–24 mm),
  C (<22 mm). Packed in 5 kg and 10 kg crates or cartons with absorbent liner
  and moisture pad; buyer branding available. Stored at 2–5 °C, 90–95% RH.
  Shelf life 21–30 days on an unbroken cold chain. About 2,000 × 10 kg
  cartons (~20 tonnes) per 40 ft reefer. MOQ: one 40 ft container by sea, or
  500 kg by air; trial lots negotiable.
- **Monthong durian (ทุเรียนหมอนทอง)** — April–August. Harvested at 80–85%
  maturity with dry-matter testing per lot. 15–18 kg cartons, foam-netted.
  Carried at 13–15 °C.
- **Mangosteen (มังคุด)** — May–September. Selected for glossy rind and fresh
  green calyx, no gamboge staining. 5 kg and 10 kg cartons. 8–12 °C.
- **Lychee (ลิ้นจี่)** — April–June. Hong Huay and Chakrapad varieties, picked
  at dawn and chilled immediately. 2 kg and 5 kg cartons with gel ice. 2–4 °C.

## How an order runs

1. **Enquiry** — buyer states fruit, grade, volume, destination and Incoterm;
   quotation returned within two working days.
2. **Sourcing** — harvest booked in advance with GAP-certified partner
   orchards, fixing price and picking date.
3. **Grading and packing** — hand-graded to the agreed spec, weighed, sealed,
   and photographed for buyer approval before loading.
4. **Documentation** — phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin,
   commercial invoice, packing list, and B/L or AWB.
5. **Shipping** — 40 ft reefer container or air freight, with tracking sent.

## Quality and logistics

- Partner orchards hold GAP certification; the packing shed follows GMP and
  HACCP practice, with lot codes traceable back to the orchard.
- Pesticide residue testing against destination MRLs: EU, China (GACC),
  Japan (MHLW). Phytosanitary certificate issued for every shipment.
- Cold chain: fruit enters the cold room on picking day; temperature logged
  throughout; data logger placed in the container on request.
- Delivery points: EXW Lamphun; FOB Laem Chabang port, or Suvarnabhumi /
  Chiang Mai airport; CFR and CIF to the agreed destination port.
- Payment: first order 30% T/T deposit with balance before B/L release;
  repeat buyers L/C at sight or 30-day T/T, case by case. Quoted in USD or
  THB. Quotations valid 7 days, because longan farm-gate prices move weekly.

## Target markets

- **China** — longan, durian, mangosteen; via the Youyiguan land crossing or
  sea port; GACC registration required.
- **Hong Kong / Singapore** — small, frequent lots, suited to air freight.
- **Europe** (Netherlands, France) — strict on MRL and SO₂ limits.
- **Middle East** (Dubai) — gifting and premium supermarket channels.

## Thai fruit harvest calendar

Peak months in brackets; national averages, with the North and the East two to
three weeks apart. Longan and mango also crop off-season from induced orchards.

- Longan — Jul–Sep [Aug], plus off-season Nov–Feb
- Durian — Apr–Aug [May–Jun]
- Mangosteen — May–Sep [Jun–Jul]
- Lychee — Apr–Jun [May]
- Rambutan — May–Sep [Jun–Jul]
- Longkong — Jul–Oct [Aug–Sep]
- Mango (Nam Dok Mai) — Dec–Jun [Mar–Apr]
- Pomelo — Feb–Mar and Aug–Nov [Sep–Oct]
- Dragon fruit — May–Oct [Jun–Jul]
- Jackfruit — Jan–May [Feb–Mar]
- Pineapple — year-round [Jan–Feb, Apr–Jun, Nov–Dec]
- Young coconut — year-round [Mar–May]
- Sweet tamarind — Dec–Feb [Dec–Feb]

## Scale and honesty note

Alpha Fresh is a small business, not a large industrial exporter. There is no
automated grading line and no in-house laboratory — residue testing goes to an
external lab, and there is a ceiling on weekly volume. Fruit is graded by hand,
which is why quality is checked crate by crate rather than sampled. Contact
some figures on the current site are placeholders in this draft; the contact
details are real.
